text.p: Tropical Storm Hannah, with 45 mph winds, is in the southern Philippine Sea near 11n/133e, moving north at 5 mph. Hannah will weaken as it turns more westward this period, likely dissipating over open water by 24-36 hours. This system will become less of a threat to shipping as it weakens.

Tropical Cyclone Pancho, with 130 mph winds, is in the southern Indian Ocean near 12.4s/93.0e, moving west-southwest at 10 mph. Pancho will continue on this track and intensify over the next 24 hours before beginning a slow weakening trend thereafter. Shipping in the vicinity of this system will continue under extreme risk for the next 48 hours.

Tropical cyclone Gretelle is becoming an increasing risk to shipping as it moves by to the north of Reunion, east of Madagascar, during the next 24 hours. Top winds of 70 mph may increase to 80 mph during this time. Gretelle is expected to continue to strengthen as it moves towards the east-central coast of Madagascar thereafter. Landfall is expected in about 48-72 hours with top winds of 90 mph likely. Strong winds and a storm surge will cause damage to coastal property at the time of landfall. We can also expect flooding rain and mudslides after the system makes landfall.
